BLOCKER: STORE-DATAFLOW.md (generated, authoritative) now classifies `secrets.json` as sensitivity `internal`, tenant `tenant`, backend `postgres`, retention `unbounded/standard`, status `migrated` — down from `secret|global|json|policy|critical|deferred`.

Same doc downgrades `provider-keys.json` from `secret-ref|policy|critical|deferred` to `internal|tenant|postgres|unbounded|standard|migrated`. The authoritative dataflow now misrepresents secret-store handling posture (retention, sensitivity, and "migrated" claims not backed by this change).
MAJOR: The doc header says "Generated from config/store-registry.json; do not edit by hand", yet the registry diff touches 11 entries while the doc changes ~200 rows and the store count 232→244 (tenant_scope/backend/retention reclassifications across unrelated stores). Registry and generated dataflow are not reproducible from each other — either the doc was hand-edited or the registry change is incomplete/hidden.

`Service.byID` queries `artifacts WHERE id=$1` with no `tenant_id` predicate; isolation depends entirely on RLS being enabled and the session GUC being set by `BindTenant`. Missing defense-in-depth on the exact path that gates idempotent reuse.

The RLS non-leakage test does not prove RLS: `svcB.Verify` failing is equally explained by a name/tenant-scoped miss ("no artifact metadata"), not by a policy denial. No direct unbound read of tenant A's row by tenant B is attempted.

No CI/Makefile/wiring for the new `go/intakeingest` module in the diff. Every DB-backed test (`TestServiceIntegration`, `TestEnsureRuntimeRoleRefusesBypass`) `t.Skip`s without `PF_RUNTIME_DSN`, so the idempotency/checksum/revision/RLS evidence required by AC can be permanently vacuous in CI.

`collect()` ingests every file under `--root`; the registry's `source_glob` values are documentation only and are never enforced or reconciled. The 11 declared entries and the actual ingest set can silently diverge while the registry asserts `status: exists`.

`objectChecksum` maps a max-bytes overflow to `Drift` with message "cannot match the source" — conflating "could not verify" with "checksums disagree", which violates the verify contract and will produce false-positive drift alarms.

`Verify` sets `res.ArtifactID = ArtifactID(tenant, bucket, name, sourceChecksum)`, so a drift result reports an artifact id that does not exist in the DB, breaking ops correlation for exactly the failure case that matters.
MINOR: The "streamed re-hash" fallback is not streamed: both `Verify` and `objectChecksum` do `io.ReadAll` into memory (up to 256MiB), doubling resident memory instead of hashing through `io.Copy`.
`isUniqueViolation` depends on `datastore` preserving `SQLState()` through error wrapping; if wrapped, concurrent-ingest retries never fire and the run fails hard instead of retrying.
`Orphans()` keys `known` by checksum only; an object shared by two logical names whose row was deleted for one name is silently reported as referenced.
`preflightWritable` truncates `--report-file` before the run; a failing run leaves an empty/partial report where consumers expect the pinned `pf.intake-ingest/1` schema.
`gate0_check.py` fail-closed change is out of scope for BI-PF-1475, untested, and will abort Gate 0 for any unreadable/unparseable changed backlog item regardless of this item's subject matter.
NIT: `logResult` discards the `json.Marshal` error and prints an empty line on failure.
`--dry-run` combined with `--verify` sets `report.dry_run=true` while `Verify` still performs DB reads.
